# TikTok

Use the shared release and receipt workflow in [publish-video](../SKILL.md).
Read [upload transport](upload-transport.md) for local-file transfer.

- Verify the uploaded filename/preview before continuing; an enabled Post button
  alone does not establish that the correct media finished uploading.
- Assess AI-generated-content settings against both picture and audio. Labels
  applied by TikTok may differ from creator-selected settings; record what is
  actually shown.
- Do not claim public availability while review or restricted visibility remains.

## Controlled caption editors

In observed Studio sessions, generic select/paste and direct DOM text assignment
could leave the displayed caption out of sync with DraftJS state or trigger an
editor error. Stop after a failed input attempt and inspect the existing draft;
do not repeatedly fill it or publish because the DOM looks correct.

If the harness permits page
scripting and inspection confirms a DraftJS editor, a narrowly scoped fallback
can use that **observed editor's existing** editorState/onChange mechanism,
preserving its decorator and editor semantics. Do not load remote scripts or
apply this method to an unrecognized editor. Verify controlled plain text,
displayed text, count and saved draft state before posting.

## Reconcile before retrying

- A newly submitted post may temporarily appear under review or restricted.
  Inspect its status later; do not create a replacement because it is not public yet.
- Content tables can virtualize rows. Use the observed table's scrolling or
  search/filter controls; absence from the first visible rows is not evidence
  that an upload failed.
- A platform or intermediary may transcode the video. Compare preview, duration
  and content; a different downloaded hash alone does not mean it is the wrong
  source. Keep the selected local source hash in the receipt.

## Official references

Checked September 21, 2026; consult current controls and guidance when they differ.

- [TikTok Studio](https://support.tiktok.com/en/using-tiktok/creating-videos/tiktok-studio)
- [AI-generated content](https://support.tiktok.com/en/using-tiktok/creating-videos/ai-generated-content)

# Transfer a local video to a browser uploader

Prefer the available browser tool's file-upload operation on an observed input;
in Voyager's browser that is `preview_upload`, which sets the file without opening the
system file picker. If that is unavailable, use its supported file chooser or the
authorized computer-control route. Browser and filesystem access may belong to different
machines: a remote browser cannot reach your machine's loopback address.

## Optional local bridge

Use this only when the browser runs on the same machine as the helper, the harness
permits page scripting, and the page/browser permits the local request. Do not
disable browser protections or bypass a denied tool/permission to make it work.

The bundled [serve-upload.py](../scripts/serve-upload.py) requires Python 3.9+.
Resolve its path relative to this skill directory. Start it in a managed terminal
session with the exact allowed page origin and only the selected video(s):

```sh
python3 /absolute/path/to/publish-video/scripts/serve-upload.py \
  --origin https://studio.youtube.com --file /absolute/path/to/final.mp4
```

For TikTok, use the exact origin observed in its uploader (commonly
`https://www.tiktok.com`), not a wildcard. It snapshots the explicit files into a private temporary folder,
prints JSON containing opaque URLs, names, sizes, MIME types and SHA-256 hashes,
and expires after 600 seconds (`--lifetime SECONDS`, at most 86400, changes that).

Compare each manifest hash with the selected source receipt **before** passing
its URL to the browser. Use only the currently observed uploader input:

1. In the permitted page context, fetch that one opaque URL and require a successful
   response. Obtain the bytes/Blob; verify its size and, when practical, SHA-256
   against the helper manifest.
2. Construct a `File` with the original name and declared MIME type. Put it in a
   `DataTransfer`, assign its files to the observed video input, and dispatch the
   uploader's normal bubbling change event. Do not submit the publishing form.

Do not use it to expose a project tree or credential
file. Stop the owned terminal session once transfer completes, including on error;
automatic expiry is a backstop. Do not move to public hosting without the task authorizing that exposure.

# YouTube and Shorts

Use the shared release and receipt workflow in [publish-video](../SKILL.md).

- Verify the **channel**, not just the signed-in Google account. One account may
  manage several channels. Match the requested channel name/handle and, when
  available, its stable ID.
- Use [upload transport](upload-transport.md) if the uploader needs a local-file
  bridge. Capture the assigned video ID and draft URL immediately, even while
  processing.
- For a requested thumbnail, use the supplied asset or
  [make-image](../../make-image/SKILL.md).
- Determine audience, promotion and synthetic/altered-content settings from this
  video's content and context. Include audio in that assessment.
- Inspect processing and the checks actually offered for this channel/video.
  Wait for relevant results by default; incomplete is not passed. If the user's
  release timing requires proceeding while a permitted check is pending, preserve
  and report that pending status. Do not dispute claims or change the media
  automatically.
- Use the URL returned by YouTube; do not manufacture a Shorts URL or assume every
  vertical video is classified as a Short.

## Recover the same upload

- If a warning interrupts Publish, inspect whether it requires returning to
  checks or acknowledges an existing submission. Stay with that video ID.
- After closing an unfinished upload, find its entry in Studio Content before
  starting again. Read its actual visibility rather than assuming the default.
- Processing can finish at different times for different resolutions. Report the
  quality actually verified; a draft preview is not proof of public playback.
- DOM text in a contenteditable is not evidence of persistence. If a permitted DOM input method is necessary, observe the
  current control, trigger its normal input behavior, and verify the saved value
  on a later step.

## Official references

Checked September 21, 2026; refresh when the UI, eligibility or policy matters to
the task.

- [Upload videos in Studio](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/57407?hl=en)
- [Synthetic or altered content disclosure](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/14328491?hl=en)
- [Visibility settings](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/157177?hl=en)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Short-lived, allowlisted local video transport; never uploads or publishes."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import mimetypes
import secrets
import shutil
import signal
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
from contextlib import contextmanager
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from pathlib import Path
from socketserver import TCPServer
from urllib.parse import urlsplit


@contextmanager
def upload_server(files, origin):
    parsed = urlsplit(origin)
    if (parsed.scheme != "https" or not parsed.hostname or parsed.username or parsed.password
            or origin != f"https://{parsed.netloc}"
            or parsed.path or parsed.query or parsed.fragment or any(c.isspace() for c in origin)):
        raise ValueError("Origin must be an exact HTTPS origin with no path, credentials or wildcard")
    if "*" in origin or not files:
        raise ValueError("Supply an exact origin and at least one explicit file")
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="voyager-upload-") as directory:
        assets = {}
        manifest = []
        for value in files:
            source = Path(value).expanduser().resolve(strict=True)
            if not source.is_file():
                raise ValueError(f"Not a regular file: {source}")
            target = Path(directory, secrets.token_hex(24))
            digest = hashlib.sha256()
            with source.open("rb") as incoming, target.open("xb") as snapshot:
                for chunk in iter(lambda: incoming.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
                    snapshot.write(chunk)
                    digest.update(chunk)
            size = target.stat().st_size
            if not size:
                raise ValueError(f"Empty file: {source}")
            mime = mimetypes.guess_type(source.name)[0] or "application/octet-stream"
            route = "/" + target.name
            assets[route] = (target, size, mime)
            manifest.append({"name": source.name, "source": str(source), "size": size,
                             "mime": mime, "sha256": digest.hexdigest(), "route": route})

        class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def setup(self):
                super().setup()
                self.connection.settimeout(10)

            def log_message(self, *args):
                pass

            def allowed(self):
                if (self.headers.get("Origin") != origin
                        or self.headers.get("Host") != f"127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_port}"):
                    self.send_error(403)
                    return False
                if self.path not in assets:
                    self.send_error(404)
                    return False
                return True

            def cors(self):
                self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", origin)
                self.send_header("Vary", "Origin")
                self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network", "true")
                self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")

            def do_OPTIONS(self):
                if not self.allowed():
                    return
                if self.headers.get("Access-Control-Request-Method") != "GET":
                    self.send_error(405)
                    return
                self.send_response(204)
                self.cors()
                self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Methods", "GET, OPTIONS")
                self.end_headers()

            def do_GET(self):
                if not self.allowed():
                    return
                target, size, mime = assets[self.path]
                self.send_response(200)
                self.cors()
                self.send_header("Content-Type", mime)
                self.send_header("Content-Length", str(size))
                self.send_header("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
                self.end_headers()
                with target.open("rb") as snapshot:
                    shutil.copyfileobj(snapshot, self.wfile, length=1024 * 1024)

        class LoopbackServer(ThreadingHTTPServer):
            def server_bind(self):
                # HTTPServer otherwise reverse-resolves loopback at startup;
                # a slow system resolver must not delay this local transport.
                TCPServer.server_bind(self)
                self.server_name = "127.0.0.1"
                self.server_port = self.server_address[1]

        with LoopbackServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler) as server:
            yield server, [{**row, "url": f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_port}{row['route']}"}
                           for row in manifest]


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--origin", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--file", action="append", required=True, dest="files")
    parser.add_argument("--lifetime", type=float, default=600)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if not 0 < args.lifetime <= 86400:
        parser.error("--lifetime must be greater than zero and at most 86400 seconds")
    # Managed terminal sessions normally stop helpers with SIGTERM. Unwind the
    # temporary-directory context instead of leaving snapshots on that path.
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, lambda *_: sys.exit(0))
    with upload_server(args.files, args.origin) as (server, manifest):
        timer = threading.Timer(args.lifetime, server.shutdown)
        timer.daemon = True
        timer.start()
        print(json.dumps({"origin": args.origin, "lifetimeSeconds": args.lifetime, "files": manifest}), flush=True)
        try:
            server.serve_forever(poll_interval=0.1)
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            pass
        finally:
            timer.cancel()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

name: publish-video
description: "Publish, draft or schedule videos on YouTube and TikTok; check existing posts."
---

Distinguish uploads, saved drafts, scheduled posts and public releases; report
only the outcome verified.

## Choose the destination and route

- [YouTube and Shorts](references/youtube.md): Studio channel identity, metadata,
  checks, visibility and playback verification.
- [TikTok](references/tiktok.md): Studio upload, controlled caption editors,
  disclosure settings and moderation status.
- [Upload transport](references/upload-transport.md): moving a local file into a
  browser uploader, including the optional bundled loopback helper.

Use an available authenticated publishing integration when it covers the task,
or the platform's Studio through available browser tools.
For a UI-only gap, use [use-computer](../use-computer/SKILL.md). Respect a selected
route such as Buffer; changing routes after a timeout requires reconciling the
existing draft/post first. Do not sign up for accounts or buy hosting as a side
effect of uploading. Hand login or authentication challenges to the user.

## Establish the release

Reuse instructions already given for account, exact cut, public text, visibility,
timing and batch scope. A request to publish now authorizes that publication; do
not add a second approval ceremony. If only preparation is requested, keep it
local. If only upload/draft is requested, do not make it public. For scheduling,
resolve the timezone and read back the platform's date, time and timezone before
saving.

Select explicit versions by content and the user's request, not modification time.
For Shorts, TikTok or Reels, run
`voyager media review FILE --platform shorts|tiktok|reels --json` before posting: fix text it flags under the platform's controls (`checks.safeArea`) or a subject cut
off by the frame edge (`checks.frameEdge`), or say why it stays.
For continuous motion, sync or how a clip sounds, use [watch and listen](../choose-media-model/references/understanding.md) (paid upload).
Write public-facing text separately from private production notes. Filenames,
internal version labels and render labels are not public titles unless requested.
Keep relevant credits; do not impose a fixed language, category, hashtag count,
audience, promotion or AI-label setting from a previous upload.

## Submit once and reconcile

Before uploading, inspect the local receipt and the target account's existing
uploads, scheduled posts and drafts. A matching title is a clue, not proof of a
duplicate: compare the source version, account, available preview and remote ID.
Resume the matching draft rather than creating a second upload. Replacing an
already public post is a separate action from uploading a revision.

Keep a small durable receipt in the current workspace at
`publishing/<platform>/receipts.json` (such as `publishing/youtube/receipts.json`), as
`{"receipts": [...]}` with one entry per account + source hash + intended release:
`file` (the local file, relative to the workspace), `sha256`, account, public
metadata, requested visibility/time, `remoteId` and `url` as soon as assigned,
`stage` (the last confirmed one: `uploaded`, `draft`, `scheduled` or `published`),
checks, `actualVisibility` and `verifiedAt`. Write `published` only once the post is
verified public or unlisted. Record submission intent before the final publish/schedule
action and its result afterward. Do not store passwords, cookies or access tokens.
For batches, track each item independently and honor partial-release instructions.

After timeout, navigation failure or an ambiguous submit, inspect the original
draft/post before retrying or switching tools. Do not infer failure from a missing
toast, start a duplicate upload, or let concurrent workers publish the same item.

Finish with public titles, links and accurate per-item states, plus any concrete
blocker. Stop temporary upload helpers.
